name: Lake Tai
note: Lake: the large freshwater lake on Wuxi's southern shore, known for its fish, pearls and lakeside scenic spots; Wikivoyage lists it as a See item.

name: Turtle Head Island
note: Peninsula park: Yuantouzhu, a 5A scenic area on Lake Tai's northwest coast, known for its cherry blossoms and lake views.

name: Grand Buddha at Ling Shan
note: Religious scenic area: Lingshan with the 88 m bronze Grand Buddha, Brahma Palace and temples, on the Lake Tai shore.

name: Nianhua Bay
note: Themed town: a Zen-themed scenic town beside Lingshan, with shops, a canal and a lake setting.

name: Xihui Park
note: Park: Xihui Park and its Old Town at the foot of Xi Shan, with Jichang Garden and the Dragon Light Pagoda on the hill.

name: Jichang Garden
note: Classical garden: the garden in the Xihui scenic area that Emperor Qianlong copied at the Summer Palace; it has its own entry fee.

name: Huishan Ancient Town
note: Ancient town: a historic street district at the eastern foot of Huishan Mountain, with ancestral halls and snack streets.

name: Donglin Academy
note: Historic site: a Ming-era academy with gardens, halls and a stone arch, where scholars prepared for the imperial exams.

name: Wuxi Museum
note: Museum: Wuxi's largest public museum, covering local history and art, and free to enter.

name: Nanchang Street
note: Ancient street: a renovated canal-side street of traditional shops and snacks beside Qingming Bridge.

name: Qingming Bridge Ancient Canal
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap area 298260074 (清名桥古运河历史文化街区)
note: Historic district: the Qingming Bridge section of the Grand Canal, a riverside old-town district that overlaps Nanchang Street.

name: Chong'an Temple
note: Temple and commercial street: Nanchan Temple (Chong'an) in Liangxi, now a cultural mall and temple-bazaar district.

name: Chinese Decorative Stone Park
note: Park: a stone-appreciation park at the north entrance of China Wu Culture Expo Park, with decorative rock displays.

name: China Wu Culture Expo Park
note: Park: a large Wuxi expo and culture park in the Wuxi New District; no visitor source fetched yet.

name: Lihu Park
note: Park: a lakeside park on Lihu Lake, built in 1927, with a long embankment, willow trees and pavilions, and the Star of Taihu Lake Ferris wheel.

name: Liyuan Garden
note: Garden: the Liyuan classical garden beside Lihu Lake, famous for Lake Tai rock formations, possibly part of Lihu Park.

name: Star of Taihu Lake
note: Ferris wheel: a water Ferris wheel by Lihu Lake; a ride, judged as a Lihu Park attraction.

name: Wuxi Zoo
wiki: Wuxi Zoo and Taihu Lake Amusement Park
note: Zoo: a National 4A zoo with more than a thousand animals, a sightseeing bus and an amusement area, in Binhu district.

name: Wuxi Sunac Land
note: Theme park: a Sunac amusement park in Binhu with a long roller coaster, operated by the Sunac group.

name: Wuxi Sunac Sea World
note: Aquarium: a Sunac Sea World marine park with sharks, rays and more than 1,500 species.

name: Wuxi Hot Snow Miracle
note: Indoor snow park: an artificial snow slope inside the Sunac Rongchuang complex, with beginner and intermediate runs.

name: Canal Bund Art Museum
note: Art museum: Canal Bund Art Museum on the Grand Canal at Hubin Road, possibly the same complex as Canal 5 Creative Campus; check.

name: First Ancient Town in Jiangnan
note: Ancient town: the First Ancient Town in Jiangnan, a large old-town scenic area on the site of the former Tai Bo residence (Meicun, Xinwu district).

name: Dangkou Ancient Town
note: Ancient town: Dangkou, Wuxi's only provincial-level historic town, in Erhu, with a scenic area.

name: Yangshan Peach Resort
note: Peach resort: Yangshan Mountain's peach orchards, known for spring peach blossom; the blossom festival is a seasonal event, the orchards are permanent.

name: Taibo Temple
note: Temple: a Ming and Qing temple complex near the entrance of Huishan Ancient Town, the largest in Wuxi.

name: Helu City Site
note: Archaeological site: remains of the capital of King Helu of Wu, a Jiangsu Grand Site; no visitor source fetched yet.

name: Hongshan Archaeological Museum
note: Museum: an archaeological museum in Wuxi New District with Wu-culture finds from the Hongshan tomb complex.

name: Wuxi Art Museum
note: Art museum: the Wuxi painting and calligraphy museum in Chong'an district; no visitor source fetched yet.

name: Wuxi Grand Theatre
note: Performing arts venue: the Wuxi Grand Theatre, a concert and theatre building; judged on whether it is open to visitors as an attraction.

name: Wuxi Mosque
note: Mosque: a Wuxi place of worship listed on Wikipedia; judged as a religious building.

name: Saint Joseph's Church, Wuxi
note: Church: a Catholic church in Wuxi listed on Wikipedia; judged as a religious building.

name: Wuxi Christian Church
note: Church: a Christian church in Wuxi listed on Wikipedia; judged as a religious building.

name: Chongshan Temple
note: Temple: a Buddhist temple in Wuxi listed on Wikipedia; judged as a religious building.

name: Plum Garden
note: Garden: the Rongshi Plum Garden in Wuxi, a private garden built by a Wuxi industrialist family; no visitor source fetched yet.

name: Ligang Power Station
note: Industrial heritage: a former power station in Wuxi; listed on Wikipedia, judged on public access.

name: Xishan Island
note: Island: a Lake Tai island off the Wuxi shore; no visitor source fetched yet.

name: Huishan National Forest Park
note: Forest park: a national forest park beside Taihu University in Wuxi's Huishan district; no visitor source fetched yet.

name: Changguangxi Wetland Park
note: Wetland park: a 10 km canal and wetland linking Lihu Lake and Lake Tai, with the Shitang Bridge; no Wikipedia article found.

name: Jin Gui Park
note: Park: a 48-hectare park in Binhu, known for spring cherry blossoms and tulips.

name: Yixing Ceramics Museum
note: Museum: the China Yixing Ceramic Museum in Dingshu, the first ceramics museum in China, showing Yixing teapots and clay ware.

name: Longchi Mountain Scenic Area
note: Scenic area: a nature reserve in the Zhangzhu hills with a bicycle park and sightseeing car, home to rare pines and magnolias.

name: Yixing Bamboo Sea
note: Bamboo forest: a national AAAA scenic area of about 667 hectares of bamboo beside a mirror lake, 31 km southwest of Yixing.

name: Shanjuan Cave
note: Cave: a limestone karst cave in Yixing with its own scenic area and tours.

name: Zhanggong's Cave
note: Cave: a limestone karst cave in Yixing that is a Taoist site with Tang-era inscriptions; the Wikipedia article title was not found.

name: Taiji Cave Scenic Area
note: Cave scenic area: Taiji Cave (太极洞风景区) in southern Yixing, a karst cave; the English Wikipedia Taiji Cave article is a different cave in Anhui, so it is not used. No visitor source fetched yet.

name: Longbeishan Forest Park
note: Forest park: a national 4A forest park in Yixing with 5.5 square km of woodland and recreation; no Wikipedia article found.

name: Tuanjiu Scenic Area
note: Lake scenic area: Tuanjiu in Yixing, a 4.5 square km area of which 60 percent is water, a Jiangnan water-town view; no Wikipedia article found.

name: Yiyuan Garden
note: Garden: Yiyuan (Yingyuan) Garden in Yixing, listed as a Yixing site on Chinatripedia; no visitor source fetched in full.

name: Yunhu Lake
note: Lake: a Yixing lake listed on Chinatripedia; no Wikipedia article found.

name: Yixing National Forest Park
note: Forest park: a national forest park in Yixing listed on Chinatripedia; may overlap Longbeishan Forest Park.

name: Guoshan Stele
note: Monument: the Stele for the Shan Sacrifice on Mount Guo, a Three Kingdoms-era stone stele in Yixing.

name: Yaohu Town
note: Scenic town: a new Yixing scenic town that began trial operation in 2025; no Wikipedia article found.

name: Ebizui Park
note: Park: a Yangtze riverside park named after its goose's-beak shape, with river views and tree-lined paths.

name: Huangshan Lake Park
note: Lake park: an ecological park centred on a lake in Jiangyin, with boating, cycling and walking paths.

name: Changjing Ancient Town
note: Ancient water town: Changjing, with canals, stone bridges and traditional architecture, southeast of Jiangyin city.

name: Feima Water City
note: Water town: a modern water-town complex in Xinqiao with canals, bridges, shopping and dining.

name: Xu Xiake's Former Residence
note: Historic residence: the Ming-era birthplace and study of the geographer and travel writer Xu Xiake, with exhibits on his travels.

name: Junshan Park
note: Park: Jiangyin Junshan Park, a historic hill park with Wu and Yue-era buildings and inscriptions.

name: Former Residence of Liu Brothers
note: Historic residence: the former home of Liu Bannong and Liu Tianhua, modern Chinese linguist and musician, with exhibits.

name: Huangshan Fort
note: Fortress: a late Qing fort in the Huangshan Scenic Area, with gun emplacements, bunkers and observation posts on the Yangtze.

name: Zhongshan Park
note: Park: a 1928 park in Jiangyin's centre commemorating Sun Yat-sen, with monuments and historical relics.

name: Huaxi Village
note: Village: a Jiangyin village listed on Wikipedia; visitor access and tourism unconfirmed.
